LESSON: READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING 3.3 Reading phrases By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners are ass
Topic 3.4: Reading comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what you read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read
2. read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING COMPREHENSION
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading comprehension helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read

What this means
In this part you learn to read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures

What this means
In this part you learn to read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading comprehension to a partner. (skill: read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read.
3. Practise this skill: read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Reading comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what you read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read aloud short texts and  Learners ask and answer simple questions related stories accurately to materials read.
5. Be able to: read at an appropriate speed for  Learners are prompted to predict meaning from enjoyment pictures.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
